title: Chicken Provencal
subtitle: Braised chicken with tomatoes, olives and Provencal herbs
excerpt: Chicken Provencal is a French braise from the south, built on tinned tomatoes, black olives, capers, and the herbs of the region. The chicken simmers slowly in the sauce until it is very tender and the sauce has thickened into something deeply savoury.
sourceNotes: Poulet a la Provencale is a classic of French regional cooking from Provence. The combination of tomatoes, olives, capers, and aromatic herbs defines the flavour profile of the region.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool fully and freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Defrost in the fridge overnight and reheat gently.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles or triples well. Use a larger stockpot and increase braising time by 10 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Tastes better the next day. Make up to 2 days ahead and refrigerate.

content.text: Brown the chicken well before adding any liquid. Colour on the skin means flavour in the sauce. Do not rush this step.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in the stockpot over medium-high heat.
Brown the chicken for 4 minutes each side until deep golden. Work in batches if the pot is crowded. Set aside.
Add the onion to the pot and cook for 5 minutes until softened. Add the garlic, paprika, thyme, rosemary, and bay leaves. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the tinned tomatoes and 150ml water. Stir and scrape any bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return the chicken to the pot. Add the olives and capers. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and simmer for 35 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has thickened.
Remove the herb sprigs and bay leaves. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve with crusty bread or rice.

items.symptom: Sauce is too thin after cooking.
items.cause: Lid was on, trapping the steam.
items.fix: Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes to reduce.

items.cause: It was not cooked for long enough at a gentle simmer.
items.fix: Cook for 10 more minutes; thighs need patience.
